requirement: Identify the governing prospective package as NCT05142280 Protocol Version 1 and its separate Statistical Analysis Plan, both dated 19 November 2021, and keep the reference plan annotation-only.

evidence.text: The protocol prints NCT05142280, 19-11-2021 and Protocol Version 1.
The independent plan prints the exact title, NCT05142280 and 19-11-2021.

requirement: Describe a prospective web-based, randomized, participant-blinded, 1:1 parallel comparison of an active-choice intervention with GP-like usual-care advice, with one questionnaire immediately after the intervention.

evidence.text: The protocol describes two randomized parallel groups, participant blinding and a questionnaire directly after intervention.

requirement: Preserve the full randomized intervention contrast: active choice includes heart age 16 years above actual age, risk explanation, four coping strategies, pros and cons and values clarification, whereas control presents a 31% ten-year CVD risk and advice to change lifestyle and take medication.

evidence.text: The arm descriptions specify different risk formats and the additional active-choice content.

requirement: Define the causal estimand as the effect of the complete bundled active-choice condition versus the complete usual-care-advice condition; do not attribute the contrast solely to choice autonomy because risk format and informational content also differ between arms.

evidence.text: The active arm receives heart age and extensive decision support while control receives a numeric ten-year risk and GP-like advice.

notes: The randomized contrast is identifiable, but the mechanism-specific interpretation is not.

requirement: Resolve the target age range before finalization: the objective says 40-65 years, while the methods and eligibility criteria specify 45-65 years; retain the protocol exclusions for prior/current CVD, preventive lipid or blood-pressure medication, diabetes, kidney damage, rheumatism, limited walking, wheelchair use and pregnancy.

evidence.text: The objective states ages 40-65 but eligibility states ages 45-65 and lists exclusions.

requirement: Treat degree of active choice, intention strength for the chosen coping behavior and commitment to that behavior as the three primary outcomes, all measured immediately after intervention.

evidence.text: The outcome table defines the measures and immediate assessment.
The SAP explicitly calls active choice, intention strength and commitment the three primary outcomes.

requirement: Score degree of active choice as the mean of its 11 five-point items only if the items demonstrate Cronbach alpha of at least 0.70; otherwise report the reliability failure and obtain a revised analysis decision rather than silently forming the composite.
acceptable_values: no silent composite if threshold fails

evidence.text: The protocol defines an 11-item five-point active-choice mean score.
The SAP forms composites only when Cronbach alpha is 0.70 or higher.

requirement: Reconcile instrument versions before scoring: the protocol table lists one intention-strength item and three commitment items, whereas the registry record lists two and five respectively; document the frozen item set, reverse coding and partial-item rule.

evidence.text: The protocol table specifies one intention-strength item and three commitment items.

notes: Official registry metadata describes two intention-strength items and five commitment items; this registry-versus-protocol conflict requires source-instrument review.

requirement: For multi-item scales, form a composite only at Cronbach alpha at least 0.70 by summing included items and dividing by their number; score autonomous motivation as the mean of the included TSRQ autonomous-motivation subscale items.

evidence.text: The SAP gives the reliability threshold, composite formula and TSRQ autonomous-subscale mean.

requirement: For participants choosing both lifestyle change and medication, use the higher of the corresponding separate item scores rather than their average for outcomes to which this rule applies, and list every affected derived variable.

evidence.text: The recoding section directs use of the highest score for participants selecting lifestyle plus medication.

requirement: Analyze degree of active choice, intention strength and commitment separately with linear regression using randomized condition as the independent variable.

evidence.text: The analysis mapping assigns each of the three primary outcomes to linear regression on condition.

requirement: Analyze the four-category coping intention outcome—lifestyle change, medication, both or no change—with multinomial logistic regression using randomized condition as predictor, and prespecify the reference category.

evidence.text: The protocol defines the four intention categories.
The SAP assigns intention to multinomial logistic regression on condition.

requirement: Analyze intentions to change diet and physical activity as two separately derived binary outcomes with logistic regression on randomized condition; define how multiple lifestyle selections and the 'other' response are coded.

evidence.text: The outcome table lists diet, physical activity, smoking and other lifestyle intentions.
The SAP specifies logistic regressions for diet and physical-activity intentions.

requirement: For the four knowledge items, combine wrong and 'don't know' responses, derive the number correct, and analyze that ordered count with ordinal regression using randomized condition as predictor.

evidence.text: The plan defines the knowledge recode and ordinal regression of number correct on condition.

requirement: Use separate linear regressions on randomized condition for self-efficacy, lifestyle response efficacy, medication response efficacy, autonomous motivation, cognitive risk appraisal and affective risk appraisal.

evidence.text: The endpoint-specific analysis list maps these outcomes to linear regression on condition.

requirement: Inspect frequencies, distributions and system-missing codes and apply pairwise deletion in each analysis; report the analysis-specific denominator and missing count rather than implying a single complete-case sample.

evidence.text: The protocol specifies pairwise deletion for missing data.
The SAP checks missingness and distributions, identifies system-missing values and excludes missing values pairwise.

requirement: Replace the data-dependent age-confounding rule with a prespecified adjustment strategy and threshold: state how confounding is assessed for the three primary outcomes, whether age enters all primary models, and how any decision propagates to secondary outcomes.

evidence.text: The SAP says to correct for age only if confounding is found and then check secondary outcomes, without a threshold.

requirement: Prespecify interaction models and decision rules for effect modification by gender, education, health condition and decision preference, including the interaction threshold and whether stratum-specific estimates are reported regardless of significance; do not use an unspecified 'if found' rule.

evidence.text: The protocol proposes gender modification and a decision-preference sensitivity analysis only if effects differ.
The SAP adds education and health condition but leaves effect-modification detection and propagation data dependent.

requirement: For decision-preference modification, classify Control Preferences Scale scores 1-2 as active and 4-5 as passive and omit score 3 from that modifier analysis; report the number excluded and do not exclude score 3 from unrelated primary analyses.

evidence.text: The SAP dichotomizes scores 1-2 versus 4-5 and excludes score 3 from the effect-modification analysis.

requirement: Define the primary efficacy population and randomized-treatment attribution, including the handling of consented but ineligible participants, randomized participants who do not view all assigned material, duplicate or implausibly rapid panel responses and participants lacking every post-intervention outcome.

evidence.text: The protocol defines eligibility, randomization and immediate assessment but no analysis set or post-randomization exclusion rule.
The SAP says to select eligible participants but does not define randomized analysis-set membership.

requirement: Define the confirmatory hierarchy and multiplicity strategy across three primary outcomes, secondary outcomes, two lifestyle-intention tests and modifier analyses; state two-sided alpha and confidence level and label analyses not protected by the strategy as exploratory.

evidence.text: The protocol defines many outcomes and additional analyses but no inferential hierarchy or multiplicity control.
The SAP lists many separate regression analyses without alpha, interval or multiplicity conventions.

requirement: For every regression, report the condition effect with an appropriate effect measure and confidence interval and prespecify coding, reference levels, linearity and residual checks, sparse-category handling, proportional-odds assessment for knowledge and fallback methods when assumptions or convergence fail.

evidence.text: The protocol names only generic linear and logistic regression.
The SAP links outcomes to models and generic assumption links but omits effects, intervals and operational fallback rules.

requirement: Use the prospective target of 724 participants—206 men and 156 women per group, 412 men and 312 women total—based on 80% power, two-sided alpha 0.05 and a 0.15-point active-choice difference assessed in men and women; do not substitute registry actual enrollment 743 for this target.

evidence.text: The prospective sample-size section gives the effect, alpha, power, sex-specific group sizes and total n=724.

requirement: Before finalization, expose unresolved implementation choices: randomization algorithm and seed retention, frozen questionnaire version, scale direction and partial-item rules, covariate coding, model reference levels, treatment-effect reporting, multiplicity, data-quality exclusions and assumption-failure fallbacks.

evidence.text: The protocol provides outcomes, computer allocation and generic methods but not these implementation details.
The brief SAP adds coding and model mapping but still leaves these operational decisions unresolved.
